name: King's Indian Attack
description: A setup-based opening course that teaches consistent development patterns and kingside safety.

branches.title: Main Line: Safe Setup
branches.description: Build the Nf3-g3-Bg2 setup against a normal Black response.

moves.title: Develop first
moves.explanation: Nf3 develops, controls central squares, and keeps the setup flexible. Nf3 develops a knight to f3. Developed pieces control central squares, help castling, and make future tactics possible without forcing anything too early.

moves.title: Black takes center
moves.explanation: Black claims central space. d5 changes the central structure. Central pawn moves should either claim space, challenge an enemy pawn, or open a line for a piece. The King Indian Attack is a setup: castle first, then prepare e4 or kingside pressure when the center is stable.

moves.title: Prepare the bishop
moves.explanation: g3 opens a safe home for the bishop and supports castling. g3 is a practical improving move for White. In real games, keep asking: is my king safe, are my pieces active, and what central pawn break comes next?

moves.title: Black develops
moves.explanation: Black improves a knight and controls e4. Nf6 develops a knight to f6. Developed pieces control central squares, help castling, and make future tactics possible without forcing anything too early.

moves.title: Fianchetto
moves.explanation: Bg2 puts the bishop on the long diagonal and prepares king safety. Bg2 develops a bishop to g2. Developed pieces control central squares, help castling, and make future tactics possible without forcing anything too early.
